topic: Entailment as a test for apposition
claim: Replacing a containing NP with its appositive is supposed systematically to preserve entailment.
evidence_summary: In We found no city of Manchester in the gazetteer, replacement by Manchester loses the quantifier.
finding: Restrict the test to suitable identifying uses. CGEL already admits name-bearing readings with indefinite matrix NPs.
inference: Does replacing the whole quantified matrix NP with the identifying name preserve entailment?

evidence.passage: §14.3, p. 447. Replacing a containing NP with its appositive is supposed systematically to preserve entailment.
evidence.example: We found no city of Manchester in the gazetteer can be true when the gazetteer contains no city bearing that name. Substitution of Manchester for the entire object produces We found Manchester in the gazetteer, which can then be false.
evidence.establishes: The loss of no breaks the entailment. The test remains available for definite identifying NPs. CGEL explicitly includes an indefinite city of Manchester on p. 448. The audit extends that name-bearing use to a negative quantifier.
evidence.locator: Structural analyses with a genuine rival
